title: Unscoped enumerations
recap: An enumeration names a closed set of domain choices. Unscoped enumerator names enter the surrounding scope, so their names must avoid collisions there.
Use meaningful enumerators to make branching readable. The behavior of a direction operation should not depend on callers remembering numeric positions.
objectives: Implement the stated behavior for multiple inputs.
Run the visible tests and explain one boundary case.
warnings: The function/type interface is fixed, but implementation syntax is your choice.
Do not remove the visible tests; the checker keeps an independent copy.
Respect the stated input domain and lifetime/range rules.
challenge: Implement turnRight(direction) for the supplied unscoped Direction enum. Rotate north -> east -> south -> west -> north. Inputs are always one of those four enumerators. Prefer a switch with named cases rather than relying on undocumented integer codes.
hints: Map each of the four enumerators explicitly.
The last direction wraps to the first.
Return a Direction value on every path.
